drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thank you. For discussion and subject to client approval, the revised draft provides for 12 months’ base salary and continued benefits following termination without Cause or resignation for Good Reason, with proposed definitions and notice and cure procedures. It also replaces the proposed post-employment non-compete with tailored confidentiality protections. The Executive’s identity, effective date, compensation, governing law and benefits-continuation mechanics remain subject to confirmation.

edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE. Subject to client approval, if the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, the Company shall pay the Executive severance equal to 12 months of the Executive’s then-current annual base salary, disregarding any reduction giving rise to Good Reason, in substantially equal installments over 12 months in accordance with regular payroll practices and subject to applicable withholding. For that period, the Company shall also continue the Executive’s then-current health and welfare benefits on the same cost-sharing basis as applies to active employees, to the extent permitted by applicable law and the applicable plans. If continued participation is unavailable, the parties shall agree upon a lawful equivalent arrangement before execution. Accrued salary and other vested entitlements shall remain payable independently of severance. “Cause” means the Executive’s fraud or embezzlement involving the Company; conviction of, or plea of guilty or no contest to, a felony involving dishonesty; or willful misconduct, gross negligence or material breach of this Agreement that causes material harm to the Company. Before terminating for Cause, the Company shall provide written notice specifying the grounds and a reasonable opportunity for the Executive to respond, together with 30 days to cure any curable conduct. “Good Reason” means, without the Executive’s written consent, a material reduction in base salary, a material diminution in duties or authority, a material relocation of the Executive’s principal workplace, or the Company’s material breach of this Agreement. The Executive must give written notice within 90 days after becoming aware of the condition, allow the Company 30 days to cure, and resign within 60 days following expiration of that cure period if the condition remains uncured. Payment mechanics remain subject to review under applicable tax and employment law.
edits.name: Proposed severance and termination definitions

edits.text: 4. CONFIDENTIALITY; NO POST-EMPLOYMENT NON-COMPETE. No post-employment non-competition restriction shall apply. The Executive shall not use or disclose the Company’s confidential, nonpublic information except in performing duties for the Company or as otherwise authorized or permitted by law. Confidential information excludes information that becomes public through no breach by the Executive, is lawfully obtained from a third party without a duty of confidentiality, or is independently developed without use of the Company’s confidential information. These obligations apply only while the information remains confidential; trade secrets shall be protected for so long as they qualify as trade secrets under applicable law. Nothing in this Agreement prohibits protected whistleblowing, reporting possible violations to governmental authorities, cooperating with investigations, making legally protected disclosures, or exercising other nonwaivable rights. No prior Company authorization or notice is required for those activities. Legally compelled disclosure is permitted, with advance notice to the Company only where lawful and reasonably practicable. This section does not restrict the Executive’s use of general skills, knowledge and experience. Any mandatory statutory notices shall be included before execution once applicable law is confirmed.
edits.name: Replace non-compete with tailored confidentiality protections
